claims.text: Role in ASD: atypical antipsychotics (eg, risperidone, aripiprazole) help ritualistic, self-injurious and aggressive behaviors.
claims.quote: There is evidence that atypical antipsychotic medications (eg, risperidone, aripiprazole) help relieve behavioral problems, such as ritualistic, self-injurious, and aggressive behaviors.
claims.locator: Treatment of Autism Spectrum Disorder › Pharmacotherapy

claims.text: Risperidone: irritability w autistic disorder (aggression, self-injury, tantrums, quickly changing moods); efficacy in 3 short-term trials, ages 5–17.
claims.quote: RISPERDAL is indicated for the treatment of irritability associated with autistic disorder, including symptoms of aggression towards others, deliberate self-injuriousness, temper tantrums, and quickly changing moods. Efficacy was established in 3 short-term trials in children and adolescents (ages 5 to 17 years)

claims.text: Aripiprazole for irritability w autistic disorder (6–17 y): start 2 mg/day; usual 5–15 mg/day.
claims.quote: Pediatric Patients (6 to 17 years) The recommended dosage range for the treatment of pediatric patients with irritability associated with autistic disorder is 5 to 15 mg/day. Dosing should be initiated at 2 mg/day.

claims.text: Risperidone cautions: in kids, assess wt gain against expected normal growth;
claims.quote: When treating pediatric patients with RISPERDAL for any indication, weight gain should be assessed against that expected with normal growth.

claims.text: raises prolactin more than other antipsychotics;
claims.quote: RISPERDAL is associated with higher levels of prolactin elevation than other antipsychotic agents.

claims.text: galactorrhea, amenorrhea, gynecomastia and impotence are reported w prolactin-elevating drugs.
claims.quote: Galactorrhea, amenorrhea, gynecomastia, and impotence have been reported in patients receiving prolactin-elevating compounds
